# Mona Visa

> Non-custodial subscription billing and agent payments on Monad. Merchants sell USDC subscriptions; subscribers approve once through Permit2 and renewals are charged automatically, straight to the merchant's wallet. AI agents pay APIs per request over HTTP 402 (x402) from prepaid sessions with spending mandates and escrow.

## What it does

- Merchants create a plan on-chain (price, period, trial, grace period), share a hosted checkout or payment link, and track subscribers, invoices and revenue in a dashboard. Their backend checks entitlements through an API key and receives signed webhooks.
- Subscribers connect a wallet and subscribe with one approval. No card, no account. They can cancel at any time. Each period the contract can charge at most the plan price plus the 1% fee.
- A permissionless keeper calls `renewMany` when periods end. Failed charges mark the subscription past due and are retried until the grace period ends.
- AI agents open a prepaid session in `SessionVault`, sign cumulative vouchers per payee, and a facilitator verifies them off-chain; a settler redeems them on-chain in batches. Hierarchical mandates cap what an agent may spend, and escrows support verify-then-settle.

## Why Monad

Per-request agent payments of a few cents and batched renewals of many subscriptions only make sense with very low gas, and sub-second blocks let a subscriber see the payment confirm on the checkout page. The rules live in contracts, so Mona Visa never holds funds.

## Fees

1% protocol fee (100 bps). On subscriptions it is added on top of the price, so the merchant receives the full price. On agent payments it is taken from the payee's share. The admin can change the rates up to a 10% cap.

## Source

- Code and README: https://github.com/justbiar/monavisa
- Stack: Solidity 0.8.30 (Foundry, UUPS proxies), TypeScript SDKs (@monavisa/core, node, react, agent, mcp), Hono API on Cloudflare Workers with D1, React + wagmi frontends.
